P.C. :
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

2. The Petitioner has alleged contempt against Respondent No.1- Mr.Swapnil Subhash Tangde breaching the order passed by this Court on 29 April 2021 in Writ Petition (ST) No.9785/2021.
3.

This petition was filed by the Petitioner seeking a direction to Respondent No.1 to decide the objections raised by the skn 2 59-CP-158.2023.doc Petitioner for disbursement of the claim of compensation in respect of the land acquired under the National Highways Act, 1956.

Before the amount was disbursed, the writ petition came up on board on 29 April 2021 and the following order came to be passed:

sentences.text: " Stand over to 9th June, 2021.
In the meanwhile, the compensation shall not be disbursed by Respondent No.1."

Thereafter the writ petition was finally disposed of by the order dated 18 February 2023, which reads thus:
"1.

By this Petition the Petitioner seeks writ of certiorari for quashing and setting aside the Order dated 2nd April 2021 passed by the Respondent No.1, thereby rejecting the application filed by the Petitioner.

It is the case of the Petitioner that the Petitioner has entered into an 'Agreement for Sale' with the predecessor of Respondent Nos.2 to 51 in respect of the property which is the subject matter of the acquisition.

2. The Petitioner has already filed a Civil Suit in the Court of Civil Judge Senior Division, Vasai being Special Civil Suit No.40 of 2012 praying for specific performance of the said 'Agreement for Sale' dated 2nd June 2007 and also registered a Notice of Lis Pendense with the Sub-Registrar of Assurances on 9th August 2012.

entities.text: Court of Civil Judge Senior Division, Vasai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. In our view, as the alleged rights of the Petitioner in the 'Agreement for Sale' dated 2nd June 2007 are not established and are subject matter of Special Civil Suit No.40 of 2012, Writ Petition filed by the Petitioner inter-alia praying for a writ of certiorari for quashing and setting aside the Order dated 2nd April 2021 is untenable and deserves to be rejected.

4. We accordingly pass the following Order:-
(a) Writ Petition No. 1639 of 2022 is dismissed.
skn 3 59-CP-158.2023.doc (b) It is made clear that the pending Civil Suit filed by the Petitioner shall be decided on its own merits.
(c) Ad-interim relief, granted by this Court on 29 th April 2021, to continue for a period of two weeks from today.
(d) It is made clear that, when this Court passed the Order of ad-interim relief on 29th April 2021, this Court has not gone into the merits of the matter.

(e) If any application for ad-interim relief is sought by the Petitioner in the pending Civil Suit or in any other independent proceedings, the same shall be decided on its own merits."

sentences.text: The Petitioner has placed on record that on 26 September 2021 the amounts were directed to be disbursed to the accounts of the claimants by Respondent No.1.
Alleging this to be a deliberate breach of the orders of this Court, the present contempt petition is filed.
5. A reply affidavit is filed on behalf of Respondent No.1 wherein explanations are sought to be given.
The fact that Respondent No.1 was aware of the order dated 29 April 2021 immediately on the next day is not disputed as he has placed endorsement to that effect in the affidavit.
The explanation is that he was under impression that the interim order is not continued and since the claimants were demanding the amounts of compensation he has bonafidely disbursed the same.

The second explanation sought to be given is that when the final order was passed a direction skn 4 59-CP-158.2023.doc was issued to freeze the accounts of the claimants and thereafter since they made representations the accounts were de-freezed.
6. Today as the consequence of the actions of Respondent No.1 is that the entire amount of compensation has been disbursed in violation of the order dated 29 April 2021.
The claimants were party Respondents in the writ petition.
It is not placed on record by Respondent No.1 that any of the Respondents- Claimants had represented before him in writing that ad-interim order passed by this Court is vacated.
This is something Respondent No.1 has done by his own, without any proper explanation.

If the Respondent- Sub Divisional Officer was not sure as to whether ad-interim order is continued or not, nothing stopped Respondent No.1 from taking guidance of the office of the Government Pleader or directing the claimants to apply to the Court for vacating the order.

7. Issue notice to Respondent No.1- Mr.Swapnil Subhash Tangde under Rule 8 of the Contempt of Court (Bombay High Court) Rules, 1994, making it returnable on 22 February 2024 at 2.30 p.m., to show cause as to why action be not taken against Respondent No.1- Mr.Swapnil Subhash Tangde.
Let the reply affidavit pursuant to the notice be filed by Respondent No.1.
 (M.M. SATHAYE, J.) (NITIN JAMDAR, J.)
